title: Modelling Josephson Junctions with Boundary Conditions: Towards High-Fidelity Models for Superconducting Qubits
authors: Luis Bueno Blanco, Juan Manuel Pérez-Pardo
abstract: Josephson junctions are the central nonlinear element of superconducting qubits, yet their standard description is reached through a chain of approximations. We propose a purely quantum-mechanical model of the junction, formulated directly in Hilbert space: a charged particle moves on a one-dimensional loop, and the junction is a point at which the wave function obeys self-adjoint boundary conditions, labelled by a coupling strength $λ$, which controls the transparency of the junction, and a phase jump $δ$, which plays the role of the superconducting phase difference. For a loop with a single junction we solve the spectral problem and show that the ground-state momentum expectation, identified with the supercurrent, factorises exactly as $\langle\hat{p}_0\rangle = I_c(δ,λ)\sinδ$. For opaque junctions $I_c$ becomes independent of $δ$ and the first Josephson relation $I=I_c\sinδ$ is recovered; for strongly attractive coupling, where the ground state is bound to the junction, the $\sinδ$ law is also recovered, but with an exponentially suppressed amplitude. For more transparent junctions, however, the model \emph{predicts} deviations from the pure $\sinδ$ law: $I_c$ acquires a dependence on $δ$ already at order $λ^{-2}$, compatible with the higher Josephson harmonics recently found necessary to describe superconducting qubit spectra, and a fully transparent contact yields a current linear in $δ$. When the phase varies in time, a gauge transformation shows that the voltage drop across the junction is proportional to $\dotδ$, so that the second Josephson relation emerges without being imposed. The boundary-condition approach thus reproduces both Josephson relations from first principles and predicts corrections to them, offering a route towards higher-fidelity models of superconducting qubits.
summary: This paper proposes a purely quantum-mechanical model for Josephson junctions by imposing self-adjoint boundary conditions on a particle moving on a loop. It successfully derives both the first and second Josephson relations from first principles. Crucially, the model predicts deviations from the simple sinusoidal current-phase relation for highly transparent junctions, offering a path to more accurate qubit Hamiltonians.
main_problem: To develop high-fidelity quantum-mechanical models for Josephson junctions, which are critical nonlinear elements in superconducting qubits, by moving beyond standard, approximate descriptions.
main_result: The purely quantum-mechanical boundary-condition approach successfully reproduces both the first and second Josephson relations from first principles and naturally predicts higher-order corrections (higher Josephson harmonics) for transparent junctions.
method: The authors formulate the problem by treating the junction as a point where the wave function must satisfy specific self-adjoint boundary conditions, solving the resulting spectral problem for the system Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a charged particle confined to a one-dimensional loop containing a single Josephson junction. The junction is mathematically defined by self-adjoint boundary conditions involving a coupling strength ($\lambda$) and a phase jump ($\delta$).
key_observables: Supercurrent ($\langle\hat{p}_0angle$), which is predicted to factorize as $I_c(\delta, \lambda)\sin\delta$; the voltage drop across the junction ($V \propto \dot{\delta}$).
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($\lambda$, controlling transparency); Superconducting phase difference ($\delta$); Critical current ($I_c$).
main_assumptions: The model is based on a one-particle Hamiltonian approach, valid in the low-carrier-density regime, and assumes the junction is a point-like interface.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical necessity of a quantum-mechanical treatment, derives the model using self-adjoint boundary conditions, analyzes the resulting current-phase relation in various limits (opaque, transparent), and demonstrates the emergence of both Josephson relations from the fundamental quantum structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, first-principles quantum framework for modeling superconducting qubits, directly addressing the need for higher-fidelity Hamiltonians by predicting non-sinusoidal current-phase relations.
